newsitem.title: THAILAND: Siam Cement says needs foreign loans.
newsitem.headline: Siam Cement says needs foreign loans.

text.p: Siam Cement Plc said on Thursday foreign commercial borrowing would remain its major source of funding despite its hefty foreign exchange losses after the sharp depreciation of the baht in the past week.

Siam Cement president Chumpol Na Lamlieng told a press conference his firm had no plan to raise capital in the near future despite its possible foreign exchange losses of up to 9.9 billion baht ($347 million) after the baht was floated.
"Our group does not need to raise capital as our operating revenue is quite sufficient for repaying debt and future business expansion," said Chumpol.

The Siam Cement chief executive declined to say how much additional debt burden his firm would face after the baht declined more than 15 percent since July 2. He said the industrial and construction materials group has an outstanding $4.0 billion foreign debt and an overall 3-to-1 corporate debt/equity ratio. Chumpol said three quarters of Siam Cement's foreign debt carried long-term maturity.
"Foreign borrowing would remain a major source of our funding despite the baht volatility because of limited availability of long-term domestic funds," he said.
Siam Cement fell six baht to 480 in late Thursday morning after it announced its foreign exchange losses.
Chumpol estimated that Siam Cement would need to raise prices of its products by five to 10 percent to reflect higher production cost brought by the baht depreciation.
He said the extent of Siam Cement's foreign exchange losses, to be reflected on its second quarter financial statement, would be determined by the baht movement.
Chumpol said if the baht firmed to 27.00 to the dollar, its losses would be pared to 2.7 billion baht but the damage would rise to 7.5 billion baht if the currency eased to 29.00 to the dollar.
The baht was traded at 28.900-29.100 late on Thursday morning.
